translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Devarim,
Shabbos Chazon,
the 4th of Menachem-Av, 5736*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through contemplating how mitzvos in this world draw down Atzmus (Awtsmoos), they become new each day.

translations.translation: “Tzion shall be redeemed through justice, and her captives through charity,”
And the Alter Rebbe brings in Likkutei Torah, the discourse beginning with this verse,
at its beginning, the statement,
“And these words that I command you today,”
that this refers to every day,
for every day they should be in your eyes as new.
And he explains,
that in order to come to this
(that every day they should be in your eyes as new),
it is through contemplating this very verse – “And these words that I command you today.”
For the coming into being of all the worlds is from the attribute of Malchus, which is only a radiation,
and through the fulfillment of the mitzvos in this world, there is a drawing down of the Essence (Awtsmoos).
For this is “that I command you today,”
“I am that I am.”
Therefore, one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world is greater than all the life of the World to Come,
for the World to Come is that they delight in the radiance of the Shechinah,
only a radiance,
and through repentance and good deeds in this world, there is a drawing down of the Essence (Awtsmoos).
And this is “that I command you today,”
specifically today,
“Today to do them, and tomorrow to receive their reward,”
for the reward of the mitzvos in the World to Come
(tomorrow)
is only a radiance,
and through the fulfillment of the mitzvos in this world,
“today to do them,”
they draw down the Essence (Awtsmoos).
And through contemplating the concept of “I command you today,”
that through fulfilling the mitzvos today
(in this world)
the Essence (Awtsmoos) is drawn down
through this, the mitzvos will be for him in the manner of “today,”
that every day they will be in his eyes as truly new.
And he continues in the discourse,
that all this is as it should be,
but when it is not so,
and his bitterness and joy are over matters of this world,
then,
the G-dly spark within him is in exile within his animal soul,
“like a sheep before its shearers is silent,”
and about this it is written, “Tzion shall be redeemed through justice, etc.”
(as will be explained below, section 9).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why contemplating the superiority of reward in the World to Come is insufficient to make mitzvos feel new, and why specifically the concept of drawing down Atzmus is needed.

translations.translation: And it needs to be understood,
for seemingly,
even when the mitzvos are like an old decree
in his eyes,
it is possible that he fulfills them with vitality,
and even,
that this
(fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos)
is the main thing for him.
And from what is said in the discourse, “but when it is not so, etc.,”
it seemingly implies
that when the mitzvos are not new in his eyes, then surely his bitterness and joy are over matters of this world.

And also, it needs to be understood what is said in the discourse, that in order to come to “every day they should be in your eyes as new,” it is through contemplating the concept of “I command you today,”
that through fulfilling the mitzvos in this world
(“today”)
there is a drawing down of the Essence (Awtsmoos)
which is vastly superior to the reward of the mitzvos in the World to Come, which is only a radiance,
for seemingly,
since the pleasure
(and delight)
from the radiance of the Shechinah in the World to Come is a very great delight
[and especially that the intent of “World to Come” here is not only the Garden of Eden but also the World of Resurrection,
for the revelation that will be in the World of Resurrection is vastly superior to the revelation of the Garden of Eden],
behold, even through contemplating the superiority of the reward of the mitzvos
(in the World to Come)
he would have great vitality in fulfilling the mitzvos,
and in the discourse it says,
that in order for the mitzvos to be in his eyes as new and not like an old decree, he must specifically contemplate the concept of “I command you today,”
the superiority of “today to do them” which is above “tomorrow to receive their reward.”
